newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-MILLER STOPS GUROV IN SECOND ROUND TO KEEP CRUISER CROWN.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-MILLER STOPS GUROV IN SECOND ROUND TO KEEP CRUISER CROWN.

text.p: World Boxing Association crusierweight champion Nate Miller battered Alexandre Gurov into three standing eight-counts to stop the Ukraine challenger at 1:54 of the second round on Saturday.
Miller, 34, was ruled the winner on the three-knockdown rule and improved to 30-4 as he won his seventh successive fight within the distance.
The 22-year-old Gurov (18-2-2) finished the first round with a swollen eye and a bloody nose but that was only the start of his troubles.
A straight right to the chin produced the first eight-count, an uppercut to the chin brought the second and two lefts to the head prompted the referee to institute his third and final count.
"That was pretty," said Miller. "I knew I could hit him with the right hand at any time. I just had to step in there."
It was Miller's fourth defence of the title he won by stopping Orlin Norris Jr in July 1995 in London and his third defence in the past year.
"I'm ready to fight anybody now," said Miller.
